panels.description: Reports whether the selected PostgreSQL server is reachable by postgres_exporter. A value of 1 means the exporter could connect successfully.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Up

panels.description: Whether the most recent postgres_exporter scrape encountered an error. A value of 0 means the last scrape succeeded.
panels.title: Last Scrape Error

panels.description: Current total number of sessions across all databases and connection states on the selected server.
panels.title: Active Sessions

panels.description: Number of non-template databases currently exposed by postgres_exporter for the selected server.
panels.title: Databases Monitored

panels.description: Combined on-disk size of all non-template databases on the selected server.
panels.title: Total Database Size

panels.description: Current total size of write-ahead log (WAL) segments on the selected server.
panels.title: WAL Size

panels.description: Breakdown of current PostgreSQL sessions by activity state such as active, idle, or idle in transaction.
panels.title: Connections by State

panels.description: Top databases by current on-disk size, excluding template databases.
panels.title: Largest Databases

panels.description: Current backend connections per database. Useful for spotting the busiest databases on the selected server.
panels.title: Connections by Database

panels.description: Longest currently running active transaction in seconds across all databases on the selected server.
panels.title: Longest Active Transaction

panels.description: Current sessions grouped by PostgreSQL wait-event type. This helps identify whether sessions are waiting on locks, IO, client, or other resources.
panels.title: Sessions by Wait Event Type

panels.description: Top databases by committed transactions per second. Uses the PostgreSQL transaction commit counters.
panels.title: Commits per Second by Database

panels.description: Top databases by rolled-back transactions per second. A rising rollback rate can indicate application errors, contention, or failed work.
panels.title: Rollbacks per Second by Database

panels.description: Current cumulative cache hit ratio by database since PostgreSQL statistics were last reset. Higher values indicate more reads are being served from shared buffers rather than disk.
panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio by Database

panels.description: Top databases by physical block reads per second. Higher values typically indicate more disk-bound activity.
panels.title: Disk Blocks Read per Second

panels.description: Average time spent reading a data block from disk, derived from cumulative PostgreSQL read-time and read-count counters since stats reset.
panels.title: Average Read Time per Block

panels.description: Top databases by temporary file write rate. Large temp usage may indicate sorts, hashes, or queries spilling to disk.
panels.title: Temporary Bytes Written per Second

panels.description: Current number of PostgreSQL locks by lock mode across all non-template databases on the selected server.
panels.title: Locks by Mode

panels.description: Databases currently holding the most locks. Useful for spotting databases with elevated concurrency or lock pressure.
panels.title: Locks by Database

panels.description: Rate of deadlocks by database. Any sustained non-zero rate deserves investigation.
panels.title: Deadlocks per Second by Database

panels.description: Top user tables by current size. This helps identify the largest tables contributing to storage usage.
panels.title: Largest User Tables

panels.description: Top user tables by estimated dead tuples. High values can indicate vacuum lag or heavy churn.
panels.title: Tables with Most Dead Tuples

panels.description: Top user tables by sequential scan rate. Persistent high sequential scan activity can be a signal to review indexing strategy.
panels.title: Sequential Scans per Second by Table

panels.description: Indicates whether the selected PostgreSQL server is acting as a primary or replica.
panels.title: Server Role

panels.description: Replication lag behind the upstream server, in seconds. On a primary this is usually 0.
panels.title: Replication Lag

panels.description: Age of the last replayed transaction in seconds. Useful when the selected server is a replica.
panels.title: Replay Age

panels.description: Current number of WAL segments retained on the selected server.
panels.title: WAL Segments

panels.description: Duration of the most recent postgres_exporter scrape against the selected server.
panels.title: Last Scrape Duration

panels.description: Configured PostgreSQL `max_wal_size` setting for the selected server.
panels.title: Max WAL Size

panels.description: Scheduled and requested checkpoint rates. A rise in requested checkpoints can indicate checkpoint pressure or WAL growth.
panels.title: Checkpoints per Second

panels.description: Estimated write throughput by write source, derived from PostgreSQL background writer and checkpoint buffer counters multiplied by block size.
panels.title: Buffer Writes by Source

panels.description: WAL archiver success and failure rate. Failed archive attempts should remain near zero.
panels.title: Archiver Activity

panels.description: Time history of total WAL size retained by PostgreSQL.
panels.title: WAL Size History

panels.description: Configured PostgreSQL `max_connections` setting for the selected server.
panels.title: Max Connections

panels.description: Configured PostgreSQL `shared_buffers` setting for the selected server.
panels.title: Shared Buffers

panels.description: Configured PostgreSQL `work_mem` setting for the selected server.
panels.title: Work Mem

panels.description: Configured PostgreSQL `effective_cache_size` hint for the query planner.
panels.title: Effective Cache Size

panels.description: Whether PostgreSQL autovacuum is enabled on the selected server.
panels.title: Autovacuum

panels.description: Whether PostgreSQL is collecting IO timing statistics. This should be enabled to make read and write timing metrics more informative.
panels.title: Track IO Timing

panels.description: Per-collector success state from postgres_exporter. A value of 1 means the collector completed successfully.
panels.title: Collector Success

panels.description: Per-collector scrape duration reported by postgres_exporter. Higher values indicate slower collector queries or heavier catalog load.
panels.title: Collector Duration
